label: HTTP Request
description: Make an outbound HTTP request (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, JSON body, custom headers). Only no answer (unreachable host, dropped connection, unreadable body) is a failure; an error status (404, 500) succeeds with `status` and `ok` carrying it. A text response comes out on `body`: a JSON object as a dict, anything else (array, scalar, non-JSON text) as its raw text. A response whose type is not text (an image, a PDF, a zip) comes out whole on `file` instead. For an API key, pick a `connection` rather than writing it in `headers`.

fields.name: value
fields.label: Header value
fields.placeholder: Bearer sk-..., or the bare key

steps: Name the header the API reads its key from (`Authorization` for most, `X-Api-Key` for some).
Paste the header's whole value, with its prefix when the API wants one (`Bearer sk-...`).

inputs.name: connection
inputs.label: Connection
inputs.description: Optional: a key the request carries in the header the connection names. Leave unpicked for an API that takes bare calls.

outputs.name: body
outputs.description: A text response: a JSON object as a dict, anything else as its raw text. Absent when the response came out on `file`.

outputs.name: file
outputs.description: A response whose type is not text (or that names no type and does not read as text), stored whole. Absent for a text response.

then.message: HttpRequest '{id}' has a `url` that is not a web address. Start it with http:// or https://.
